14: # SKILL.md File Templates - Creation Guide
15: 
16: Templates for creating SKILL.md files with proper structure, frontmatter, and required sections.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines for SKILL.md (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:
63: - ✅ YAML frontmatter with required fields
64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 2. FRONTMATTER REQUIREMENTS
77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |
83: | `description` | ✅ | Single line, **≤ 130 chars** for skills (≤ 110 for commands), 1,536-char hard cap | `"Handles X when Y occurs"` |
84: | `allowed-tools` | ✅ | Array: `[Tool1, Tool2]` | `[Read, Write, Edit, Bash]` |
85: | `version` | ✅ | 4-part X.Y.Z.W | `1.0.0.0` |
86: 
87: > **Hard rules**: not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside the skill's `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects that the dispatch preflight reads.
88: 
89: > **Description budget & trim style**: see [`frontmatter-templates.md` § Description Budget & Trim Style](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md).
90: > Keep total project descriptions under the ~6,400-character ceiling. This leaves headroom below the 8,000-character auto-discovery limit.
91: > Drop product and stack lists. Drop marketing prose. Keep the skill name, primary verb, domain noun and mode suffixes (`:auto` or `:confirm`).
92: 
93: ### Template
94: 
95: ```yaml
96: ---
97: name: sk-example
98: description: Example workflow skill demonstrating proper frontmatter format with specific capabilities, use cases, and key differentiators for AI agent discovery.
99: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
100: version: 1.0.0.0
101: ---
102: ```
103: 
104: ### Key Rules
105: 
106: - **name**: Must match folder name exactly, hyphen-case only
107: - **description**: Third-person voice, single line, no `<>` brackets
108: - **allowed-tools**: Use brackets `[...]`, not comma-separated string
109: - **hard rules**: Not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects the dispatch preflight reads.
110: 
111: > **Complete Reference**: For validation rules, edge cases, array formats, and all document type frontmatter, see [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md)
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 3. SKILL TEMPLATE (WITH BUNDLED RESOURCES)
116: 
117: **Use for**: Skills with bundled resources (references, scripts, or assets)
118: 
119: **Target**: 800-2000 lines (SKILL.md <1000 lines, rest in resources)
120: 
121: **Size Constraints** (package_skill.py validation):
122: - Max 5000 words (3000 recommended)
123: - Max 3000 lines
124: 
125: **Required Sections**: WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES (with ✅ ALWAYS, ❌ NEVER, ⚠️ ESCALATE IF), REFERENCES (or combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES`)
126: 
127: Packaging enforcement note:
128: - `package_skill.py` fails if `REFERENCES` is missing and no approved combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES` structure exists.
129: 
130: **Recommended Sections**: SUCCESS CRITERIA, INTEGRATION POINTS, REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES
131: 
132: ### Template
133: 
134: ```yaml
135: ---
136: name: example-skill
137: description: Example skill demonstrating proper template structure with specific capabilities for semantic code search and context preservation workflows.
138: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
139: version: 1.0.0.0
140: ---
141: ```

33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.

35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines for SKILL.md (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:

45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)

47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:

53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:

64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73: 
74: ---
75:

77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |

9: 
10: # sk-design-diagram
11: 
12: > Draw a self-contained `.html` diagram, architecture, sequence, ER, Gantt, and 23 more types, against one shared editorial design system with a complexity budget and a taste gate, or redraw an existing draw.io / Mermaid source at the format, size, and detail level the destination needs.
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
17: 
18: | Aspect | What you get |
19: |---|---|
20: | **Use it for** | A component diagram, decision flow, data model, timeline, or any of 27 technical/product diagram types that should look custom, not templated |
21: | **Invoke with** | `/design:diagram` or the keywords "diagram", "architecture diagram", "sequence diagram", "draw.io", "mermaid" |
22: | **Works on** | 27 diagram types (generate), `.drawio*` / `.mmd` / `.mermaid` sources (import), and PNG/SVG export of a generated diagram |
23: | **Produces** | A single self-contained `.html` file: inline SVG, inlined CSS, no external images, no required JavaScript |
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. OVERVIEW
28: 
29: ### Why This Skill Exists
30: 
31: A generic AI-drawn diagram is easy to spot: dark mode with a cyan glow, identical rounded boxes for every node, a legend floating inside the drawing area, diagonal connectors crossing at odd angles. It looks technical without a single real design decision behind it. `sk-design-diagram` exists so a diagram starts from a real editorial design system, one accent color, a 4px grid, mandatory orthogonal connectors, a complexity budget, instead of freehand SVG, and never ships without running the same taste gate that catches those failure modes before delivery.
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: `sk-design-diagram` picks the right one of 27 diagram types for what's being shown, loads that type's layout conventions and complexity budget, draws against the shared design system in `references/foundations/style-guide.md`, and runs the `SKILL.md` §6 SUCCESS CRITERIA gate before handoff. It also redraws an existing draw.io or Mermaid source, extracting the structural content only, never the source's coordinates, colors, or renderer layout, at a chosen format, size, detail level, and audience. It produces standalone `.html` diagrams for the `html-svg` format, or a plain markdown flowchart for the `ascii-markdown` format: the two formats live in this one packet; the earlier separate `sk-create-flowchart` skill has been fully deprecated and removed.
36: 
37: ### When To Use This Skill
38: 
39: Reach for `sk-design-diagram` when a reader will learn more from a visual than from prose, a table, or a bulleted list. Pick `--output-format html-svg` for a standalone HTML/SVG artifact, or `--output-format ascii-markdown` when the deliverable is an ASCII flowchart embedded directly in a markdown document: both output formats live in this one packet. Skip it entirely when a short bullet list or a 3-column table already says the same thing.
40: 
41: ### The 27 Diagram Types
42: 
43: | Category | Types |
44: |---|---|
45: | **Components + connections** | Architecture, IT current-state, high-level, data flow, DP integration, DP security matrix |
46: | **Behavior + flow** | Flowchart, sequence, state machine, process, swimlane |
47: | **Data structure** | ER / data model, medallion |
48: | **Structure + ranking** | Nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, pyramid / funnel, quadrant, venn, loop |
49: | **Time + quantity** | Timeline, Gantt, bar, line, scatter, radar |
50: 
51: Full selection guide with per-type reference links: `SKILL.md` §1.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. QUICK START
56: 
57: **Step 1: Pick the right type for what you're showing.**
58: 
59: ```text
60: Draw an architecture diagram: frontend, backend, database, Redis cache.
61: ```
62: 
63: That request maps to `references/types/type-architecture.md`.
64: 
65: **Step 2: Draw the diagram against the design system, then run the taste gate.**
66: 
67: The taste gate is the `SKILL.md` §6 SUCCESS CRITERIA checklist: self-applied, no external script: type fit, the remove test, signal (accent on ≤2 elements), the five mandatory connector rules, the accessible-SVG contract, and typography.
68: 
69: **Step 3: When redrawing an existing draw.io or Mermaid file, extract first: never render.**
70: 
71: ```bash
72: python3 scripts/drawio_extract.py path/to/diagram.drawio
73: python3 scripts/mermaid_extract.py path/to/diagram.mmd
74: ```
75: 
76: Each prints the same structural digest shape: nodes, edges, containers, hubs, and budget flags. Redraw from that digest, then report the fidelity ledger: what was merged, collapsed, or dropped.
77: 
78: ---
79: 
80: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
81: 
82: Every build follows the same order. Detect the request shape, generate, import, or export.
83: 
84: - **Generate:** run the style-guide gate on the first diagram in a new project, load the matching `references/types/type-<name>.md`, and draw against the shared design tokens and that type's complexity budget.
85: - **Import:** route by source extension to `references/import-export/import-drawio.md` or `references/import-export/import-mermaid.md`, extract the structural IR with the matching script, set the four output dials (format, size, detail, audience), and redraw: never invent a component to fill a layout: never silently drop one.
86: - **Export:** extract the `<svg>` node and emit PNG and/or SVG; export is always manual: never automatic.
87: 
88: Every path ends at the same taste gate before delivery.
89: 
90: ### Key Concept: The Taste Gate Is Not Optional Polish
91: 
92: `SKILL.md` §6 SUCCESS CRITERIA is not a style nicety. It catches the failure modes that make a diagram look AI-generated instead of intentional: a diagonal connector between off-axis nodes, an arrow label sitting on top of its own line, two connectors sharing a stroke path, a legend floating inside the diagram, an accent color used on five "important" things instead of one or two. A diagram that looks right at a glance but never ran through this checklist has not actually been checked. The packet's own success criteria treat a diagram that skipped the taste gate as unfinished, not finished-with-an-unrun-check.
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
97: 
98: ### Related Skills
99: 
100: | Skill or scope boundary | Relationship |
101: |---|---|
102: | `create-quality-control` | Audits or scores an existing document. `sk-design-diagram` is for authoring a new diagram artifact. |
103: | Application / product UI work | `sk-design-diagram` is scoped to standalone technical/product diagrams, not application interfaces. |
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## 6. TROUBLESHOOTING
108: 
109: | What you see | Why | Fix |
110: |---|---|---|
111: | Diagram looks generic or "AI-drawn" | Dark mode + glow, identical boxes, no real accent decision | Re-run the §6 SUCCESS CRITERIA Signal checks; pick 1-2 genuinely focal elements |
112: | Diagonal connector between two boxes | Off-axis nodes connected with a straight `<line>` instead of an orthogonal elbow | Route with a rounded right-angle connector (`r=8`); see `SKILL.md` RULES |
113: | Arrow label unreadable or overlapping the line | Missing the mandatory 6-10px gap or opaque mask rect | Add the mask rect and the visible gap per the connector-rules checklist |
114: | Import redraw looks nothing like the source | Wrong output dial (format/size/detail/audience) for the destination | Re-check the four dials in `references/foundations/output-spec.md` against where the diagram is going |
115: | Fidelity ledger missing after an import | Redraw delivered without reporting what was merged, collapsed, or dropped | Every import must end with the fidelity ledger: see `references/import-export/import-drawio.md` / `import-mermaid.md` |
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## 7. FAQ
120: 
121: **Q: Why HTML/SVG instead of Mermaid or a design tool?**
122: 
123: A: Self-contained HTML with inline SVG opens in any browser with no renderer, build step, or account. If the deliverable specifically needs an ASCII flowchart in markdown, pass `--output-format ascii-markdown`; if it needs pixel-level product UI, that is out of scope for sk-design-diagram.
124: 
125: **Q: What if my content doesn't fit any of the 27 types?**
126: 
127: A: Pick the closest one and adapt it: the type references are layout-convention guides, not rigid templates. If you're combining two types, pick the dominant axis rather than hybridizing grammars.
128: 
129: **Q: Can this skill fetch my website automatically to onboard my brand colors?**
130: 
131: A: No: the packet has no network-fetch tool. Onboarding is agent-mediated: the calling AI session fetches the URL with its own tools and this skill maps the result to semantic tokens. See `references/foundations/onboarding.md`.
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## 8. VERIFICATION
136: 
137: | Check | Result |
138: |---|---|
139: | Package structure | `python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/validate_skill_package.py .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-diagram --strict` exits 0 |
140: | Connector rules | Every delivered diagram passes all five mandatory connector rules in `SKILL.md` RULES |
141: | Accessible SVG | `role="img"`, `aria-labelledby`, first-child `<title>`, `<desc>`, and diagram/variant-prefixed IDs on every delivered SVG |
142: | Import fidelity | Every import redraw reports a fidelity ledger, merged, collapsed, dropped |
143: | Manual review | The diagram reflects real source content, stays within its type's complexity budget, and passes the full §6 SUCCESS CRITERIA taste gate |
144: | Corpus check | `node scripts/check-diagram-corpus.cjs` from the packet root prints `RESULT: PASSED` |
145: | Outside delivery | `node scripts/check-diagram-corpus.cjs --extra <dir>` prints `RESULT: PASSED` over a delivered `.html` written outside the packet |
146: 
147: ---
148: 
149: ## 9. SCREENSHOTS
150: 
151: Every form in this mode is rendered to a PNG under
152: [`screenshots/`](./screenshots/), mirroring the source layout, so a form can be
153: judged without opening a browser.
154: 
155: Regenerate after changing any form:
156: 
157: ```bash
158: node ../shared/scripts/render-screenshots.cjs \
159:   ./assets ./screenshots --full-page   # each form at its own height
160: node ../shared/scripts/render-screenshots.cjs \
161:   ./assets ./screenshots --check   # every source covered
162: ```
163: 
164: The captures sit beside `assets/` rather than inside it: a leaf is something a mode
165: loads into context, and a picture for a human to read is not one.
166: 
167: The colour scheme follows the host machine. Chrome ignores the scheme flags in
168: headless capture, so a regenerated set matches whichever theme the operator's
169: system is set to. Both themes are valid corpus output and each is validated on its
170: own, so regenerate on the machine whose theme you want committed.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 10. RELATED DOCUMENTS
175: 
176: | Document | Purpose |
177: |---|---|
178: | [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md) | Authoritative packet contract, design system and taste gate |
179: | [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) | Machine router: intent map, resource map and loading levels |
180: | [`references/foundations/style-guide.md`](./references/foundations/style-guide.md) | Design tokens: the single source of truth for colors, typography, and spacing |
181: | [`references/foundations/output-spec.md`](./references/foundations/output-spec.md) | The four import/export dials: format, size, detail, audience |
182: | [`references/import-export/import-drawio.md`](./references/import-export/import-drawio.md) | draw.io redraw procedure |
183: | [`references/import-export/import-mermaid.md`](./references/import-export/import-mermaid.md) | Mermaid redraw procedure |
184: | [`references/import-export/export.md`](./references/import-export/export.md) | PNG/SVG export procedure |
185: | [`references/types/type-architecture.md`](./references/types/type-architecture.md) | Example of a per-type layout-convention reference |

The packet's own success criteria treat a diagram that skipped the taste gate as unfinished, not finished-with-an-unrun-check.

## 3. SURFACE STANDARDS (the non-negotiables)

- **CDN runtime reality.** Client scripts ship over a CDN with cache lag; treat every deploy as versioned and verify the minified runtime, not just the source. See `references/deployment/minification-guide/overview-terser-and-patterns.md` and `references/verification/verification-workflows/gate-and-automated-options.md`.
- **Interaction-gated loading.** Heavy vendors (HLS.js, FilePond, Swiper) load on interaction/visibility, never eagerly. See `references/performance/interaction-gated-loading.md` and `references/implementation/observer-patterns/mutation-and-intersection.md`.
- **Core Web Vitals are a gate, not a report.** LCP/CLS/INP regressions block; remediate against `references/performance/cwv-remediation.md` and `references/performance/webflow-constraints.md`.
- **Focus and forms are accessibility-load-bearing.** Focus traps and upload flows follow `references/implementation/focus-management/selector-and-focus-trap.md` and `references/implementation/form-upload-workflows/overview-architecture-and-filepond.md`.

## 4. ASSETS (on-demand, deferred from the first slice)

- Integrations, patterns, templates, scripts — `assets/integrations/`, `assets/patterns/`, `assets/templates/`, `assets/scripts/`
- Surface checklists — `assets/webflow-debugging-checklist.md`, `assets/webflow-verification-checklist.md`

Assets are pulled on demand by the active workflow phase; they are not part of the initial evidence slice.

# webflow Surface — Frontend Evidence

**Domain evidence** and shared workflow doctrine for browser/Webflow frontend work. This surface owns the implement -> debug -> verify phases through the workflow references below, and acts on the evidence gathered here when the hub detects a Webflow surface. Detection markers: `src/2_javascript`, `webflow`, `--vw-` custom properties, CDN-delivered client scripts.

## 1. WHEN THE HUB BUNDLES THIS

- The task touches Webflow-published pages, CDN-delivered `webflow.js`/client scripts, or `src/2_javascript` sources.
- The active workflow phase needs frontend standards (CSS/HTML/JS), an implementation pattern, a performance remediation, a deployment step, or a browser debugging/verification procedure.
- This surface owns edits, tests, and verification through the workflow references; hand off formal findings-first review to `code-review` and author-side quality gates to `code-quality`.

## 2. REFERENCE MAP

Language standards (load the detected language's trio; a frontend task legitimately spans all three):
- CSS — `references/css/style-guide.md`, `references/css/quality-standards/patterns-and-naming-enforcement.md`, `references/css/quick-reference.md`, `references/css/patterns/tokens-state-machine-and-triggers.md`

- JavaScript — `references/javascript/style-guide/overview-naming-and-structure.md`, `references/javascript/quality-standards/init-dom-error-and-async.md`, `references/javascript/quick-reference.md`

- Core: `implementation_workflows.md`, `webflow_patterns.md`, `animation_workflows.md`
- Async & observers: `async_patterns.md`, `observer_patterns.md`
- Forms & focus: `form_upload_workflows.md`, `focus_management.md`
- Media & vendors: `third_party_integrations.md`, `swiper_patterns.md`

## 3. SURFACE STANDARDS (the non-negotiables)

- **CDN runtime reality.** Client scripts ship over a CDN with cache lag; treat every deploy as versioned and verify the minified runtime, not just the source. See `references/deployment/minification-guide/overview-terser-and-patterns.md` and `references/verification/verification-workflows/gate-and-automated-options.md`.
- **Interaction-gated loading.** Heavy vendors (HLS.js, FilePond, Swiper) load on interaction/visibility, never eagerly. See `references/performance/interaction-gated-loading.md` and `references/implementation/observer-patterns/mutation-and-intersection.md`.
- **Core Web Vitals are a gate, not a report.** LCP/CLS/INP regressions block; remediate against `references/performance/cwv-remediation.md` and `references/performance/webflow-constraints.md`.
- **Focus and forms are accessibility-load-bearing.** Focus traps and upload flows follow `references/implementation/focus-management/selector-and-focus-trap.md` and `references/implementation/form-upload-workflows/overview-architecture-and-filepond.md`.

## 4. ASSETS (on-demand, deferred from the first slice)

- Integrations, patterns, templates, scripts — `assets/integrations/`, `assets/patterns/`, `assets/templates/`, `assets/scripts/`
- Surface checklists — `assets/webflow-debugging-checklist.md`, `assets/webflow-verification-checklist.md`

Assets are pulled on demand by the active workflow phase; they are not part of the initial evidence slice.

## 1. OVERVIEW

There is no separate template directory and no separate example directory, because the distinction
was never real. A worked diagram is the best starting point there is — it shows a convention applied
rather than described, and adjusting one is faster than filling a blank. So the library holds both
kinds side by side and neither is precious: 27 canonical diagrams, one per type, 7 variants that
demonstrate a specific pattern, and 4 starters for when you want the skin without the drawing.

Nothing here is a strict template. Change the data, the labels, the geometry, the node count. The
corpus check holds six things a file can be read for:

- accessibility wiring
- the 4px grid
- arrow-label mask clearance
- unique ids
- no external resources
- the palette block on the four starters whose tokens have to match the palette source

It says nothing about what you draw, and it leaves whether connectors meet their targets, overlap, or
fan too close together to the judged reads in the capture review.

The four starters are named `starter-light`, `starter-dark`, `starter-terminal` and `starter-full`.
They are the only forms that carry a palette block for every role, because they are what a new
diagram is copied from; a worked form keeps the tokens it actually draws with. They answer no
question of their own, which is why the catalog does not index them.

Inside a starter the drawing references its roles by name rather than by value, so repainting the
block repaints the figure. One role is declared without being drawn with: the full starter carries
`paper-2` for the framed variant that ships commented out, so uncommenting four lines sits the figure
on a card. A role declared for a documented opt-in is the one good reason to declare a role the
drawing does not use. Three of the four ship an empty placeholder drawing, so there is nothing
in them to repaint until you draw it — that is what makes them starters. The full one carries a
worked figure, and theming it moves every mark.

To repaint any of these in another visual language, see
[`../../references/design-md-theming.md`](../../references/design-md-theming.md).

## 1. OVERVIEW

There is no separate template directory and no separate example directory, because the distinction
was never real. A worked diagram is the best starting point there is — it shows a convention applied
rather than described, and adjusting one is faster than filling a blank. So the library holds both
kinds side by side and neither is precious: 27 canonical diagrams, one per type, 7 variants that
demonstrate a specific pattern, and 4 starters for when you want the skin without the drawing.

Nothing here is a strict template. Change the data, the labels, the geometry, the node count. The
corpus check holds six things a file can be read for:

- accessibility wiring
- the 4px grid
- arrow-label mask clearance
- unique ids
- no external resources
- the palette block on the four starters whose tokens have to match the palette source

It says nothing about what you draw, and it leaves whether connectors meet their targets, overlap, or
fan too close together to the judged reads in the capture review.

The four starters are named `starter-light`, `starter-dark`, `starter-terminal` and `starter-full`.
They are the only forms that carry a palette block for every role, because they are what a new
diagram is copied from; a worked form keeps the tokens it actually draws with. They answer no
question of their own, which is why the catalog does not index them.

Inside a starter the drawing references its roles by name rather than by value, so repainting the
block repaints the figure. One role is declared without being drawn with: the full starter carries
`paper-2` for the framed variant that ships commented out, so uncommenting four lines sits the figure
on a card. A role declared for a documented opt-in is the one good reason to declare a role the
drawing does not use. Three of the four ship an empty placeholder drawing, so there is nothing
in them to repaint until you draw it — that is what makes them starters. The full one carries a
worked figure, and theming it moves every mark.

To repaint any of these in another visual language, see
[`../../references/design-md-theming.md`](../../references/design-md-theming.md).

214: `--all` the form is written with its stock bytes and the note says so.
